Subject: Sandbox -> Prod bridge: initial asks

Hi Priyom,

We are targeting next Wednesday for a limited sandbox->prod bridge to validate the attachment path for our inference tenants. Can you share a short deployment runbook and a canary traffic plan? Key asks from our side:
- Minimal blast radius: how we isolate tenant traffic and fall back to hosted variant on failure
- Network verification steps (BGP, routes, NAT, MTU checks)
- Observability gates and rollback triggers

We'd like something we can hand to infra and SRE to run as a checklist. If possible, include expected maintenance windows and contact points.

Thanks — Matt

Senior Infra Eng, ClientCorp
matthew.green@clientcorp.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Green <matthew.green@clientcorp.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, acme.ops@acmecloud.com, ingrid@edgeops.io
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox -> Prod bridge: initial asks

Matt — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a concise runbook and the canary traffic matrix. TL;DR below, full runbook attached (sandbox-prod-bridge-runbook-v1.pdf).

Summary (high level):
- Objective: Verify tenant traffic egress/ingress and control-plane callbacks for a single Customer slice before broad rollout.
- Scope: 1 tenant slice in sandbox bridging to a mirrored prod tenant node (no DB writes to prod systems; config-only path).
- Canary plan: 4-step ramp; 10% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over ~4 hours with 15–30m steady-state checks. See canary-traffic-matrix.csv for exact bucket mapping.
- Rollback triggers (any one): token error rate >2% over 5m, tail latency p99 > 1.5x baseline for 10m, KV cache miss spike > 3x baseline, control-plane auth failures > 0.5%.
- Networking prechecks: MTU validation, BGP peer UP with route propagation confirmed, route leak checks, NAT mapping sanity. Network checklist file attached.

Action items for ClientCorp infra:
1) Whitelist these ports on prod edge: 443, 10250 (control-plane TLS), 9000-9010 (inference tunnels)
2) Provision a service-account with scoped permissions for the bridge runners
3) Share BGP session output and traceroute to the mirrored node before canary start

Requests for Redwood:
- Neha: confirm NAT/egress path and any SNAT implications for tenant IPs
- Tessa: prepare dashboards (latency, error rate, kvcache hitrate) + a pager runbook
- Jonas: validate control-plane fallback policy (if bridge fails, traffic should auto-failover to hosted endpoint with header X-RW-Fallback: true)

Attachments (stubs): [attachment: sandbox-prod-bridge-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: canary-traffic-matrix.csv (csv)], [attachment: network-checklist.txt (text)]

Proposed window: Wed Oct 14 02:00–06:00 UTC. If that works we'll lock it and schedule a 30m pre-run call.

--
Priyom Das
Lead, Deployments 
Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Sandbox -> Prod bridge: initial asks

Folks — forwarding Matt's request and the runbook I sent. Short internal checklist below; please reply with clear ACKs by EOD so we can lock the window.

Neha — NAT / route note: confirm if SNAT mapping for bridge runners will rewrite source tenant IPs; if yes, we need a translation table documented in runbook and observability tags to map back. Also confirm whether we need to open ephemeral ports for tunnel keepalives.

Tessa — dashboards: include these charts for canary: overall request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, auth failure count, kvcache hitrate (per-tenant), and ingress BGPRoutes accepted. Add synthetic probe that performs a full request path.

Jonas — control-plane: validate that when bridge control-plane returns 5xx for >5m we flip traffic to hosted endpoint and that the fallback header is set. Also verify KV cache affinity doesn't cause cross-tenant leakage during partial routes.

Quoted for context:
> On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 09:05 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Matt — thanks for the clarity... (runbook attached)

I expect short replies. If anyone sees an operational risk that requires postponement call it out.

-priyom
